search_log.method: Inspected the Unicode Roman critical text and recorded only individually named persons with explicit parentage, marriage, fostering, tutelage, or directly attested narrative roles.

notes: The file concentrates on the named relationships in 1.66–1.80 and dialogue figures in 1.81–1.88; 1.62–1.65 are not expanded because they contain few securely named genealogical individuals.
Repeated references to Śukra/Kāvya/Uśanas are represented by the existing Śukra node; the epithet is recorded as a label only where relevant, not as a separate person.
Names in collective or plural lists whose members are not individually named (Dakṣa’s sons/daughters and unspecified dynastic descendants) were not expanded into persons.
Mārtaṇḍa is retained as a separate named person from Vivasvat because the cited verse calls him Yama’s son; no identity merge is made.
Pāñca and Uddhava follow the BORI electronic reading of 1.70.28; their forms are not silently normalized.
The dialogue with Aṣṭaka, Pratardana, Vasumanas, and Śibi does not itself establish that they are descendants of Yayāti; only explicit parentage in the passage is encoded.
Shared node IDs for Aṅgiras, Kaśyapa, Dakṣa, Śakra, Vivasvat, Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Indra, and Marīci reuse existing Ādiparvan 1.59–1.61 batch nodes.

The 1.70.40–42 verses enumerate named solar figures as Vivasvat’s sons, then identify Mahya as the youngest and give the branch Mahya → Devabhrāṭ → Subhrāṭ → three sons. These names are preserved separately because the text gives them as a plural genealogy; no alternate-name identities are inferred.
